sampling_model.design: One aggregate unit is assigned by a known sequential kernel \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\); the comparison class includes deterministic, history-dependent, and outcome-adaptive rules.
sampling_model.units: A single fixed finite-population trajectory of length \(T\); no unit, outcome, or state is sampled from a superpopulation.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(W_t\in\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\) is randomized over time, and assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity condition is imposed on the minimax policy class. The constructive Markov design has homogeneous-history exposure probability exceeding \(1/(2\mathrm e)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no stochastic outcome nuisances. The known quantities are \(T\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(\beta\); unknown-index adaptation is outside scope.

body.tldr: The sole novel root contribution is a policy-uniform common-null multiscale occupancy--information certificate for one-unit switchbacks with fixed bounded potential outcomes, known polynomial memory index, and arbitrary outcome-adaptive assignment. A horizon-eight block-and-arm-specific-band family makes the required support, separation, posterior uncertainty, and adaptive likelihood cancellation directly falsifiable. Audited supporting results inherited or sharpened from the banked predecessor provide the Markov truncated-Horvitz--Thompson upper rate \(T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), the \(C=0\) parametric boundary, and the operational oracle window. Closing the certificate without a dyadic loss yields the matched all-policy MSE frontier.

project_justification.gap: Finite-order minimax switchback theory, geometric-mixing analyses, and recent sequential rerandomization do not supply a policy-uniform common-null information certificate for fixed-array polynomial memory. The banked predecessor already supplies the oracle upper architecture but leaves its lower bound at the no-carryover rate because its two cadence certificates are not complementary.
project_justification.niche: Known \(\beta\) isolates the oracle design problem from adaptation and turns cadence into a clean nonparametric information tradeoff: exposure variance grows with the homogeneous-history window, while deterministic carryover bias decays polynomially.
project_justification.fill: The project makes the common-null sequential multiscale certificate the single new solve target, anchored by an explicit horizon-eight block-and-band likelihood calculation. The inherited Markov upper bound, no-memory boundary, and operational window are audited supporting results; they become a matched frontier only through the new certificate.

body.related_work: Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao provide the fixed-population minimax architecture and finite-order regular-switchback benchmark; this project inherits that upper-bound architecture and does not claim it as new. Hu and Wager study geometrically mixing Markov dynamics, whose stochastic contraction does not imply a fixed-array polynomial-memory converse. Jia, Kallus, and Yu supply a truncated-exposure estimation template under rapid mixing and graph clustering, informing the supporting bias--variance audit but not the new all-policy certificate. Duchi and Ruan's AISTATS 2021 constrained-risk inequality is a decision-theoretic tool applied only after close adaptive trajectory laws have been built; it contains no switchback occupancy result. Zeng and coauthors study sequential rerandomization under no or first-order carryover, which motivates the full feedback-policy quantifier but does not deliver a worst-case polynomial-memory lower bound. Xiong, Chin, and Taylor inform the operational interpretation of windows and phases. Lin and Ding and Liu and Zhong delineate separate inference questions. The only claimed new root is the common-null multiscale occupancy--information certificate; the frontier is its downstream consequence, and no cited comparator is claimed to be tightened.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The horizon-eight family verifies a local algebraic fact only: under the displayed adaptive policy, the assignment likelihood cancels exactly; alternating paths hide the lag-one arm-specific bands, while constant paths retain opposite-arm block uncertainty. It does not establish that one member has the required risk for every adaptive path law or that dyadic aggregation is lossless. The exhaustive diagnostic through \(T\le16\) found no constant-order violation of the tested random-offset block-versus-arm-specific-band proxy on sparse-switch, strict-alternation, unequal-periodic, one-switch, and concatenated-cadence paths, but the exact divergence constants and averaging step remain unproved. The model is the pointwise bounded-difference envelope; replacing it by a weighted total-variation budget would strengthen the class restriction and change the oracle power. A necessary logarithmic factor must be reflected in the frontier.
body.honest_scope: The policy-uniform common-null multiscale certificate, its explicit lower constant, and the resulting matched frontier are open; the no-log target is not assumed. The Markov upper construction, the \(C=0\) boundary, and the operational window are inherited or sharpened supporting results recorded for audit and downstream use, not independent novelty claims. The horizon-eight construction is a falsifiable diagnostic lemma rather than the general certificate. No unknown-\(\beta\) adaptation, confidence interval, phase-selection theorem, or leading-constant claim is included.
